title: Compatibilities of Weil equivariance
statement:
All geometric- and scheme-Frobenius equivariance squares of
[thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace] and of
[prop-pur-weil-equivariance-scheme-frobenius] commute with finite
reduction, scalar extension, composition, and base change.

proof.text:
Use precisely the geometric and coefficient setting of the two statements in the conclusion: a smooth separated geometric fiber $f:X\to Y$ of the finite-type $k_0$-morphism, with strict datum $(K,\varphi_K)$. All comparison diagrams below retain their stated constructible finite-Tor domains. The smooth purity maps in the named squares have the domain of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], in particular separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$. This domain is inherited from those maps; it is not deduced from separation of $f$. All corners in the coefficient and geometric comparison diagrams remain in their named maps' domains. We use the coefficient/composition/base-change compatibility of [sk-thm-purity-transport] and the trace compatibility of [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] on exactly this domain. Write $G_T=Lg_{T,\gamma}^*$, $P_fK=Lf^*K(d)[2d]$, $F_f=Rf_!$, $E_f=Rf^!$, $a_f=\gamma_{f,K}$, and $t_f=\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{f,K}$. The purity isomorphism of [sk-thm-purity-transport] and the purity square of [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace] give the identity
$$\varphi_{E_fK}=a_f\circ\varphi_{P_fK}\circ(G_Xa_f)^{-1}.$$
The trace definition [def-pur-smooth-trace] gives $t_f=\epsilon_f\circ F_f(a_f)$, hence
$$\epsilon_f=t_f\circ F_f(a_f^{-1}).$$
At higher coefficients this formula is its coefficient transport, with the trace transport specified in [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity]. Finally [def-pur-compact-support-transport] says that the datum on $F_fM$ is $F_f(\varphi_M)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,g_\gamma}$. Thus the exceptional datum and the counit are recovered from purity, trace, the source datum and compact-support exchange, rather than being additional unproved coherence assertions.

source.place: Proof, constituent purity/counit/trace: solve the purity and trace identities

proof.text: The source datum is the two-arrow composite of [def-pur-tate-datum]: $\varphi_{P_fK}=(Lf^*\varphi_K\otimes\tau_d)[2d]b_{f,K}$, where $b_{f,K}:G_XP_fK\cong(Lf^*G_YK\otimes^LG_X\Lambda_X(d))[2d]$. In particular $b$ precedes the Tate datum. Apply [lem-pur-weil-tate-datum-transport] to this exact source: its coefficient and pullback equations identify the source data under the comparisons in the conclusion, and its composition clause identifies the iterated source with the $(d+e)[2d+2e]$ source. This is an assertion about pullback and twists, without using equivariance of the orientation.

source.place: Constituent source datum (replacement of old Step 2, first part)

proof.text: For the geometric-Galois square apply [lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing] with $g=g_{Y,\gamma}$. It identifies the actual exchange in [def-pur-compact-support-transport] with $G_YRp_*j_!\cong Rp'_*\bar g^{-1}j_!\cong Rp'_*j'_!G_X$, and supplies its coefficient and vertical/horizontal isomorphism-pasting equations on strict towers before $R\lim$. Thus the compact-support datum $F_f(\varphi_M)e_f$ has these same comparisons, by functoriality. On $k$-linear squares the matching coefficient and pasting equations are those of [fix-lem-exchanges]. No application of its $k$-linear hypothesis to a semilinear arrow is made.

source.place: Constituent compact-support datum (replacement of old Step 2, second part)

proof.text: For $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ with $1\leq m\leq n$, apply derived reduction to the three squares. The coefficient compatibility of [sk-thm-purity-transport] identifies the reduced $a_f$ with the level-$m$ purity map; [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] identifies the reduced $t_f$ with the level-$m$ trace. The composition/base-change identifications are the corresponding compatibilities of the same purity and trace statements. The operation comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] and the exchange comparisons checked in Steps 2--3 (using [fix-lem-exchanges] on its $k$-linear domain) identify the pullback/tensor terms and the compact-support exchange. A strict integral datum reduces to its specified finite datum by [def-pur-tate-datum]. For integral-to-finite reduction the same two all-coefficient statements identify $a_f$ and $t_f$ with their specified finite maps. Substitute these identities and the source identity from Step 2 into Step 1: since a functor sends $a_f^{-1}$ to the inverse of its image, the reduction of $\varphi_{E_fK}$ is the prescribed exceptional datum, and the reduction of $\epsilon_f$ is the prescribed counit. The formula for the compact-support datum then identifies every vertical arrow as well. Hence reduction takes each entire equivariance square, with its labelled arrows, to the required reduced square. This uses the cited reduction identities, not an inference that equality of ordinary derived morphisms is detected by their reductions.

source.place: Proof, finite reduction, including integral-to-finite reduction

proof.text: For scalar extension use the coefficient compatibility of the natural purity isomorphism in [sk-thm-purity-transport], including rationalization and finite field extension. The normalized traces commute with these coefficient transports by [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity]. The operation comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] and the exchange comparisons checked in Steps 2--3 (using [fix-lem-exchanges] on its $k$-linear domain) identify the remaining factors in Steps 1 and 2. Applying the scalar functor to those two formulas therefore gives the formulas over the extended ring. More explicitly, for any comparison $s$ between the two purity sources and $e$ between the two exceptional targets, $e\,T(a_f)=a'_f s$ implies $T(a_f^{-1})e^{-1}=s^{-1}(a'_f)^{-1}$; substituting this into $T(t_f\circ F_f(a_f^{-1}))$ is precisely the counit comparison, and substituting into the first formula in Step 1 is the exceptional-datum comparison. The compact-support formula then gives the remaining vertical arrows. At $\mathcal O_E$ use the completed coefficient category, at $E$ its scalar localization, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ a common finite field stage, exactly as prescribed by [def-pur-conventions]. No discrete non-torsion etale category is substituted. This proves scalar compatibility of the three geometric squares.

source.place: Proof, scalar extension and rational/common-stage passage

proof.text: Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow hZ$ be smooth, of dimensions $d,e$. Step 2 identifies $P_{hf}$ with $P_fP_h$ as source data, with twist $\tau_d\otimes Lf^*\tau_e=\tau_{d+e}$. At finite coefficients [thm-pur-composition-coherence] gives $a_{hf}=c_{h,f}^{-1}a_{f,E_hK}P_f(a_h)$; at the remaining stages use [sk-thm-purity-transport]. Naturality of $a_f$ lets the $f$- and $h$-purity squares paste to this composite. The trace formula of [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] applies the $f$-trace at $P_hK$ before the $h$-trace. The vertical-pasting clause of [lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing] identifies the compact-support datum on $F_hF_f$ with that on $F_{hf}$. Consequently pasting the two trace squares gives the $hf$-trace square with the full $e$-twist retained.

source.place: Composition: purity, source and trace pasting (old Step 5)

proof.text:
For completeness compute the counit comparison, rather than inferring it from an unspecified transport. The purity composition equation of the preceding step gives $a_{hf}^{-1}=P_f(a_h^{-1})a_{f,E_hK}^{-1}c_{h,f,K}$. Naturality of $t_f$ at $a_h^{-1}:E_hK\to P_hK$ gives $t_{f,P_hK}F_fP_f(a_h^{-1})=a_h^{-1}t_{f,E_hK}$. Substitute these two equalities and trace transitivity from [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] into $\epsilon_{hf}=t_{hf}F_{hf}(a_{hf}^{-1})$ from Step 1. After $F_{hf}\cong F_hF_f$, the result is
$$\epsilon_{hf}=t_hF_h(a_h^{-1})F_h\bigl(t_{f,E_hK}F_f(a_{f,E_hK}^{-1})\bigr)F_hF_f(c_{h,f,K})
=\epsilon_hF_h(\epsilon_{f,E_hK})F_hF_f(c_{h,f,K}).$$
The composite-adjunction counit is exactly this pasted counit by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], after the displayed exceptional-composition identification. Each equality uses naturality or the factors compared in Steps 1--3 and 6, so it preserves their equivariance squares.

source.place: Composition: inverse-purity cancellation and identification of the pasted counit (old Step 5)

proof.text: For a Cartesian base change $(u:X'\to X,v:Y'\to Y,f,f')$ with the compatible finite-field data, put $Q=Lu^*$ and $Q_Y=Lv^*$. Let $B_P:QP_f\cong P_{f'}Q_Y$ and $B_E:QE_f\cong E_{f'}Q_Y$ be the specified comparisons. At finite coefficients [thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence] gives $B_EQ(a_f)=a'B_P$, where $a'=a_{f',Q_YK}$; at integral and field coefficients use the base-change clause of [sk-thm-purity-transport]. Trace base change is [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity]. Step 2 supplies the source-datum equation $B_PQ(\varphi_P)=\varphi'_P G_{X'}(B_P)$. For compact support, [lem-pur-weil-basechange-semilinear-pasting] identifies the two orders of geometric base change and semilinear Frobenius exchange, with the canonical pullback compositors inserted. This is the mixed pasting needed here, including its strict-tower assertion, rather than an instance of $k$-linear exchange pasting applied outside its domain.

source.place: Base change: source, purity, trace and mixed exchange comparisons (old Step 6)

proof.text:
Let $B_F:Q_YF_f\cong F_{f'}Q$ be compact-support base change. Trace compatibility from [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity], naturality of $B_F$ at $a_f^{-1}$, and the inverse of $B_EQ(a_f)=a'B_P$ give the three substitutions
$$\begin{aligned}
Q_Y(\epsilon_f)&=Q_Y(t_f)Q_YF_f(a_f^{-1})\\
&=t_{f'}F_{f'}(B_P)B_F(P_fK)Q_YF_f(a_f^{-1})\\
&=t_{f'}F_{f'}(B_PQ(a_f^{-1}))B_F(E_fK)\\
&=\epsilon_{f'}F_{f'}(B_E)B_F(E_fK).
\end{aligned}$$
The last line also uses $\epsilon_{f'}=t_{f'}F_{f'}((a')^{-1})$ from Step 1. Thus the counit uses the same base-change identifications as purity and trace; the mixed exchange identity in Step 8 identifies all compact-support data in these equalities. This proves geometric base-change compatibility without enlarging any comparison domain.

source.place: Base change: counit naturality and inverse-purity cancellation (old Step 6)

proof.text:
Finally use [prop-pur-weil-equivariance-scheme-frobenius]: on every object $N$ replace $\varphi_N$ by $u_N=\varphi_N\kappa_N$. The naturality and pullback-composition compatibility of $\kappa$ are the explicitly typed comparison in [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius] and the pullback-naturality identity of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback]. To check explicitly that this replacement respects the coefficient comparisons too, recall its coefficient-independent site construction: the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site], combined with the scheme/Galois factorization, induces $\kappa$. On a weakly etale site object the trivialization is restriction along its relative Frobenius isomorphism. A change of coefficients commutes with this restriction: on a tensor representative both orders send $x\otimes b$ to $r^*(x)\otimes b$. The same restriction maps are natural under pullback of site objects; equivalently the relative Frobenius formula is $(F_U,u)$ and commutes with every map of such objects. Thus they give the same pullback-composition comparisons stated in [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. Apply the functor of coherent inverse systems and its derived limit for the integral coefficient transport, and then the scalar-localization/common-stage functors: functors preserve this equality. This is equality of the specified transformations before these functors are applied, not an appeal to faithfulness of finite reduction. For any arrow $a:N\to M$, naturality gives $G(a)\kappa_N=\kappa_M L\Phi^*(a)$, so
$$a\,u_N=a\varphi_N\kappa_N=\varphi_MG(a)\kappa_N=\varphi_M\kappa_M L\Phi^*(a)=u_M L\Phi^*(a).$$
Apply this identity to every arrow and comparison in Steps 4--10. It identifies their transported geometric squares with the scheme-Frobenius squares, proving all four compatibilities for them as well. No Cartesian base-change theorem is applied to the generally non-Cartesian scheme-Frobenius square.
